items.x_text:
AGENTS.md hijack: Forever Security found agents run from ~/Downloads obeying a malicious instruction file: 90% success against OpenAI Codex in tests. A CLAUDE.md variant exposed Claude Code's OAuth token. Start agents in the project folder.

#AISecurity #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
One text file in your Downloads folder. Your AI coding agent does what it says. 🤖

Forever Security traced a hijack on a customer's computer:
→ A coding agent tried to install a malicious npm package, function-color
→ The cause: an AGENTS.md file in ~/Downloads, which was also the agent's working directory
→ Against OpenAI Codex, a harmless test payload worked 90% of the time
→ A CLAUDE.md variant redirected Claude Code's API traffic and exposed its OAuth token
→ Claude Code alone launched 1,300+ sessions from Downloads across their customers
→ The researchers: "There is nothing here for OpenAI or Anthropic to patch."

What to do: never use Downloads as an agent's working directory, start agents in the project root, review unfamiliar AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md files, and keep approval prompts and sandboxing on.

cover.hook: From today, Sweden's government offices block ChatGPT and Claude.
cover.sub: Staff get Microsoft Copilot instead. The reason given: information security.

slides.title: What changed
slides.body: From Monday 26 Oct, the browser versions of ChatGPT and Claude are blocked on work computers at Regeringskansliet, Sweden's Government Offices: the Prime Minister's office and the ministries.

slides.title: The reason
slides.body: Digitalisation director Mikael Wettercrantz wrote that using AI services without a formal contract can affect information security, and that there had been several examples of problematic use of open AI services.

slides.label: AI services in "widespread and risky" use at one agency
slides.note: Internal audit at Sweden's Transport Administration, per Decrypt

slides.title: Not just one office
slides.body: Sweden's Tax Agency and the National Board of Institutional Care already block consumer AI tools, and the Enforcement Authority is preparing a decision. Copilot stays because it was reviewed and its security settings raised.

slides.title: Do this week
items: List the AI tools your staff actually use
Approve one tool under a proper contract
Block or monitor consumer AI sites on work devices
Tell staff what never goes into a prompt

items.question: Does your organisation have a contract for the AI tool your staff use most?

items.send_to: the person who patches your firewalls

cover.hook: Two ransomware gangs, one VPN flaw, no MFA in the way.
cover.sub: Unit 42 links Qilin and INC to CVE-2026-0257 in PAN-OS and Prisma Access. A patch has existed since May.

slides.title: The flaw
slides.body: CVE-2026-0257 (CVSS 7.8) is an authentication bypass in Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS and Prisma Access that can let attackers set up unauthorized VPN connections. Patched in May 2026; in CISA's KEV catalog since 13 May.

slides.title: Who is using it
slides.body: Unit 42: "Ransomware operators exploiting CVE-2026-0257 include Spikey Scorpius (aka Qilin) and Tarnished Scorpius (aka INC)." ReliaQuest has also reported Qilin and Settra exploiting it.

slides.title: After the VPN
slides.body: Unit 42 describes remote-management tools for recon and RDP/SMB to move around. In one case attackers went from the VPN gateway to vCenter, disabled ESXi controls and dumped a domain controller's disk offline.

slides.label: patch available. Unit 42 updated its warning in October
slides.note: Sectors hit include education, healthcare, government and energy

slides.title: Do this week
items: Confirm every PAN-OS gateway runs a fixed release
Hunt for VPN sessions you can't tie to a real user
Alert on new logins to vCenter and ESXi

items.question: Would you notice a VPN session that never passed MFA?
items.x_text:
CVE-2026-0257: Unit 42 says Qilin and INC ransomware operators exploit this PAN-OS / Prisma Access auth bypass to set up VPN sessions and get past MFA, then pivot to vCenter. Patched since May. Check your gateways.

#Ransomware #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
Two ransomware gangs. One VPN flaw. MFA didn't stop them. 🔓

Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 on CVE-2026-0257:
→ An authentication bypass in PAN-OS and Prisma Access (CVSS 7.8) that can open unauthorized VPN connections
→ Exploited by Spikey Scorpius (aka Qilin) and Tarnished Scorpius (aka INC), Unit 42 says
→ After getting in: recon with remote-management tools, RDP and SMB to move around
→ One case went from the VPN gateway to vCenter, then dumped a domain controller's disk offline
→ Patched in May 2026 and in CISA's KEV catalog since 13 May

items.x_text:
Siemens Software Center CVE-2026-110936 (CVSS 8.4) exploited: ClickFix attackers drop a malicious DLL beside a genuine signed copy (3.5.8.7) via a fake MSI. Siemens links it to the Romulus campaign. Update to 4.0.9.8.

#PatchNow #CyberSecurity
items.ig_caption:
A genuine, signed Siemens app. Loading someone else's malware. ⚠️

Siemens warns Software Center is being abused in ClickFix attacks:
→ CVE-2026-110936 (CVSS 8.4): version 3.5.8.7 loaded helper files from its own folder without checking them
→ A fake installer, AllMyBasic.msi, puts a malicious DLL next to the signed app
→ Siemens links the activity to the Romulus ClickFix campaign; Forescout tied that platform to LegionLoader, which can steal Chrome data
→ Siemens says none of its systems or update channels were breached, to its knowledge
→ Reported by Huntress Labs; fixed in 4.0.9.8

What to do: update to 4.0.9.8 or later and launch it, download only from Siemens, hunt for SiemensSoftwareCenter.exe started by msiexec from AppData, and never paste commands a web page asks you to run.
